summary.headline: Zaggle FY26 standalone revenue rose about 42% to INR1,853 crores, but FY27 standalone growth guidance slows to 25-30% as DICE moves to an asset purchase.
summary.overview: Management reported record FY26 results, with standalone revenue of about INR1,853 crores (up 42%) and PAT of about INR133 crores (up 52%). Q4 standalone revenue was about INR593 crores (up 44%) with reported EBITDA of about INR55 crores. The DICE acquisition was restructured from a 100% share purchase (originally INR123 crores) to an asset purchase for about INR68 crores excluding GST, which moves its costs onto the standalone P&L. Management withheld EBITDA guidance until integration completes, and cash flow is now the top priority, with operating cash flow about minus INR6 crores in the quarter.

segments.name: Zaggle core (Save, Propel, Zoyer)
segments.commentary: Program fees were about 41% of revenue and SaaS about 2% in FY26. Zoyer and BROME drove a significant rise in interchange fees. Management is deliberately reducing redemption-led Propel models that absorb cash, and expects Propel margin to recover toward about 5.5% from about 4% in Q4.

segments.name: 86400 (formerly Mobileware)
segments.commentary: Revenue rose from about INR34 crores in FY25 to about INR74 crores in FY26 (up 118%). EBITDA rose from about INR5.4 crores to about INR18 crores and PAT from about INR1.6 crores to INR11 crores, driven by UPI volumes and new bank partners.

segments.name: GreenEdge
segments.commentary: Revenue rose from about INR36.5 crores in FY25 to about INR103.7 crores in FY26 (up about 184%). EBITDA rose from about INR3.4 crores to about INR11 crores and PAT from INR2.1 crores to about INR8.1 crores. Standalone revenue growth of 40-50% is projected for FY27.

segments.name: Zagg.money (formerly Rio.Money)
segments.commentary: New acquisition for retail credit cards on UPI and TPAP. Management reports an annualised run rate of about 36,000-40,000 new cards, with a base of about 25,000 cardholders. Revenue is referral fees and interchange share with no balance-sheet risk.

segments.name: TaxSpanner (to be rebranded Z.tax)
segments.commentary: Management said performance was unsatisfactory last year. Rebranding and a Tax AI copilot launch are planned for Q2 FY27, and Quesscorp partnership covers a base of 5 lakh-plus users.

segments.name: DICE (asset purchase)
segments.commentary: Acquired as a spend management suite, IP and enterprise contracts for about INR68 crores excluding GST, against an original INR123 crores share-purchase valuation. DICE was loss-making in FY25 and likely in FY26; FY25 revenue was about INR10 crores, with FY26 described as significantly higher. Around 100-plus team members join.

guidance_outlook: FY27 standalone revenue growth guided at about 25-30%; consolidated growth at about 40%.
EBITDA guidance deferred to 'the next few months' until DICE integration completes, since DICE costs now sit on the standalone P&L.
Medium-term guidance of 14-15% over five years is maintained, with margin ramp of roughly 1 percentage point a year expected to be temporarily disrupted.
Five-year goal of INR500 crores revenue and INR65 crores EBITDA reiterated.
Operating cash flow expected to turn positive in coming quarters; cash flow named the top priority, followed by revenue growth and margin expansion.
US operations now targeted by fiscal year-end (FY27), pushed back from June 2026; UAE expansion on hold pending regional peace.
Propel margin expected to return to about 5.5% in coming years.
Employee and other costs likely to rise in the next quarter as DICE staff are onboarded.
capex_capacity: Capitalised development costs rose to about INR56 crores in H2 FY26 from about INR30 crores in H1 FY26; about INR107 crores capitalised in total, mostly manpower, for new product development only.
Management declined to give a FY27 capitalisation estimate, citing AI-driven investment needs for global products.
Short-term borrowing of about INR40-50 crores taken to deploy capital quickly; a INR10 crores loan to DICE was fully adjusted against the INR68 crores payout.
Management intends to deploy QIP proceeds over coming quarters for M&A and growth.
EffiaSoft acquisition dropped after reassessment of strategic need.
demand_pricing: Around 3.9 million active users on Zaggle cards and software; more than 3,900 corporate customers.
Marquee wins in Q4 include Rebel Foods, Saurashtra Cement, Blue Star, Fanuc, Generali Central Insurance, Federal Bank and others; cross-sell to Hexalog, GMR and CNH International.
Cashback and incentives are about 68% of revenue per an analyst cited metric; management said it will dial these down over time as spend management matures, and does not give GTV splits.
Fleet management and forex products are early-stage; Adani, Think Gas and AGP Pratham cited as customers, with OMC contracts still being pursued.
Management says the 2026 credit card business is growing faster than initial expectations, with card acquisition the lead indicator before spend-led revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Why are capitalised development costs nearly doubled, and does free cash flow better reflect earnings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said only new product development is capitalised, not maintenance, and it will track operating and free cash flow more closely.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Propel margins fall from about 10% to 4% YoY in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to the full-year margin of about 6% and said it is exiting redemption-heavy Propel models that absorb cash, sacrificing some margin; it expects about 5.5% in coming years.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 standalone growth guided at 25-30% after 42% in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the much larger base (about 5-6x since IPO) and a deliberate cash-flow focus that may slow Propel Points growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why did trade receivables rise from about INR40 crores to INR129 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to split receivables by business, said the net receivable position was negative about INR33-34 crores at end-September and is now close to breakeven, and cited trade receivables as one cash lever.

qa_highlights.question: Why is consolidated operating cash flow about minus INR52 crores versus about minus INR6 crores standalone?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the subsidiaries are nascent businesses recently acquired, with investments made and efficiency gains to come.

qa_highlights.question: Does DICE dilute the EBITDA run rate and the 11-12% margin path?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said DICE's impact is no worse than originally envisaged, with costs now on standalone P&L; it was loss-making and EBITDA guidance will follow integration.

qa_highlights.question: Is Propel worth keeping given its low net revenue and working-capital use?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Propel is a feeder for cross-sell and stickiness, about 90% of spend sits in program fees, and cash and ROCE optimisation is under way.

risks_watch: Operating cash flow remains negative (about minus INR6 crores standalone; about minus INR52 crores consolidated) and receivables have risen sharply.
DICE integration may lift employee and other costs in the next quarter, with EBITDA guidance still pending.
Propel margin compression and cutbacks in cashback and redemption models could slow growth and affect customer retention.
Overseas expansion (UAE and US) is delayed by regional conflict; the US launch slipped to FY27 year-end, and the company has no on-ground presence in the Middle East.
CFO role is interim after Aditya Kumar Grandhi's departure; a permanent CFO is expected soon.
Discrepancies in call figures (for example standalone FY26 EBITDA of INR181 vs INR183 crores and a GreenEdge growth percentage correction) should be checked against the filed results.

key_quotes: We are minutely focused on improving the cash flow and bringing it to a high positive level.
But we believe we are going to be able to come back to around 5.5% margins in the coming years while we improve on the cash flow.
So, we'll come back with the EBITDA guidance in the next few months once we are able to complete the integration process.
Our overall guidance of 14% to 15% over the course of next 5 years remains.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, AI and the global roadmap, and on the cash-flow pivot, but cautious on guidance: EBITDA guidance is withheld until DICE integration completes, and management declined to quantify capitalisation, DICE margin impact, cross-sell potential or cash-back reduction timelines. Evasive on receivables split, cash-back and GTV splits, and the other-current-assets breakdown, and it repeatedly declined to give ballpark spend estimates.

growth.why: FY27 standalone revenue growth guided at about 25-30% (consolidated about 40%), backed by marquee Q4 wins, card acquisition ramp and GreenEdge 40-50% growth outlook, but no specific capacity or order numbers; EBITDA guidance withheld until DICE integration completes.
